BLOCKER: Language rule: design_pack.tooling=false, yet new Python operations (compile_web_console, validate_customer_package) are added to core/packaging.py; new shipped logic must be Go, or the item must be reclassified/dispositioned as tooling before Gate 1.5.
MAJOR: Runtime gzip + Cache-Control: immutable with no declared Vary: Accept-Encoding (or ETag/If-None-Match strategy) risks shared-proxy cache misdelivery/poisoning and full re-downloads; no test asserts Vary.
IP guard misses source maps: vite *.map files embed original TS/JSX source and bypass the .ts/.tsx/.jsx extension scan; design must pin build.sourcemap=false and fail closed on *.map (AC-3).

Rollback flag ("serve external static directory") is absent from config_contract (only eap_registry, embed_fs_seach, console_dist_dir); the approved rollback cannot be configured or verified as specified.
MINOR: Scope drift: affected_files lists go/web/console_test.go but design_pack.scope omits it (CL-016 scope separation).
Determinism (NFR) incomplete: no pinning of Node/vite toolchain versions or lockfile for reproducible content hashes.
Guard data_rules cover only .ts/.tsx/.jsx and node_modules; AC-3 "zero Node.js runtime dependencies" also implies package.json, lockfiles, .tgz/.pnpm artifacts, and .mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs extensions.
Traversal boundary protection claimed in design security but has no negative test in test_matrix/implementation_controls.
Checksum manifest verification point versus go:embed build order is unspecified; a stale dist could embed if pipeline ordering is not enforced.
AC-1 negative test test_web_console_corrupt_hash_fails appears in implementation_controls but not in traceability/test_matrix, leaving the AC-1 failure path untraceable.
NIT: Per-request gzip may challenge the sub-ms NFR for large bundles; consider precompressed assets, a minimum-size threshold, and skipping already-compressed types (images, woff2).
Consider standard security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff) for the embedded SPA in the same handler.
SUMMARY: Design is structurally sound with fail-closed guards, hashed immutable caching, and AC↔test traceability, but the language-rule disposition on core/packaging.py and the Vary/sourcemap correctness gaps must be resolved before approval.
Top risks: source-map IP leakage defeating AC-3, intermediary cache misdelivery from missing Vary: Accept-Encoding, and an undeclared rollback configuration path.
